title: What Is Leech Jar? — Definition

title: Origins and History of Leech Jar
body:
The Leech Jar belongs to the 1800s–1900s era and traces to Various.

Laënnec's wooden stethoscope (1816) let doctors hear the chest; the binaural version (1851) perfected it. Ether anesthesia (1846) and Lister's antisepsis (1867) made surgery survivable; X-rays (1895) made the body visible — early tubes burned operators before safety. The iron lung (1928) breathed for polio patients; the heart-lung machine (1953) enabled open-heart surgery. Apothecaries weighed grains and drams on hand balances; patent-medicine showmen sold hope in bottles. Nursing (Nightingale, Civil War) professionalized care; the thermometer and sphygmomanometer quantified the body.

Within that longer story, Leech Jar: The 1820s' millions; the 1900s' decline. The jar is the leech's home.

title: How Leech Jar Works
body:
Acoustic devices channel body sounds: the stethoscope's chestpiece diaphragm/bell couples vibrations to air columns in the binaurals. Ether inhalers vaporized anesthetic over gauze or in closed masks. Iron lungs sealed the body in a chamber, alternating pressure to move the chest wall. Early X-ray used Crookes tubes with no shielding — fluoroscopy glowed live. Apothecary balances compared unknown powders against grain weights with knife-edge pivots. Cupping and leeching drew blood on humoral theory — now historical practice, not recommendation.

Applied to the Leech Jar (1800s–1900s, Various): The jar is the leech's home.

Clean brass and glass gently; replace perished rubber tubing with modern equivalents. X-ray tubes are display-only — never energize. Document provenance; medical artifacts carry ethical weight — collect respectfully.

title: Leech Jar — Apothecary unit converter (Runnable Python)
body:
Converts historical apothecary weights (grains, scruples, drams, ounces) to metric — the units every prescription used before grams.

The program below is real, runnable Python 3. Save it as demo.py and run `python3 demo.py`. It models the core mathematics of the Leech Jar so you can experiment with the parameters yourself.
code:
# Apothecary <-> metric converter (public-domain historical units)
# 20 grains = 1 scruple; 3 scruples = 1 dram; 8 drams = 1 ounce (480 grains)
GRAIN_G = 0.06479891

def apothecary_to_g(oz=0, dr=0, scr=0, gr=0):
    grains = oz*480 + dr*60 + scr*20 + gr
    return grains * GRAIN_G

def g_to_apothecary(g):
    grains = g / GRAIN_G
    oz = int(grains // 480); grains -= oz*480
    dr = int(grains // 60); grains -= dr*60
    scr = int(grains // 20); grains -= scr*20
    return oz, dr, scr, round(grains, 1)

print("2 drams 1 scruple =", round(apothecary_to_g(dr=2, scr=1), 2), "g")
print("5 g =", "%doz %ddr %dscr %.1fgr" % g_to_apothecary(5))
print("1 grain =", GRAIN_G*1000, "mg  (aspirin tablet ~5 grains)")
